claim: 2P-FLIM provides high spatial and temporal resolution to image murine and human cell types, 2D and 3D cell cultures, and biopsies in vitro and in vivo.
source: 2P-FLIM provides high spatial and temporal resolution to image murine and human cell types, 2D and 3D cell cultures, and biopsies in vitro and in vivo (Skala et al., 2007, Okkelman et al., 2019, Neto et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies that demonstrated these capabilities.

claim: 2P-FLIM allows reduced nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD(P)H) and flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD+) to be studied and quantified, giving insight into cellular metabolism.
source: 2P-FLIM allows reduced nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD(P)H) and flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD+) to be studied and quantified using 2P-FLIM, giving insight into cellular metabolism (Lakowicz et al., 1992; Skala et al., 2007, Neto et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to studies that established this methodology.

claim: NAD(P)H is noted as having a long fluorescence lifetime when enzyme-bound and a short fluorescence lifetime when free in the cytoplasm.
source: NAD(P)H is noted as having a long fluorescence lifetime when enzyme-bound and a short fluorescence lifetime when free in the cytoplasm.
evidence: This is established knowledge about NAD(P)H fluorescence properties.

claim: NADH and NADPH fluorescence properties are identical.
source: NADH and NADPH fluorescence properties are identical, and hence NAD(P)H refers to these intracellular pools combined (Huang et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a study that established this property.

claim: M1 macrophage phenotype is defined by secretion of a significant amount of pro-inflammatory cytokines: TNFα and IL-1β enhanced endocytosis and ability to kill intracellular pathogens.
source: M1 macrophage phenotype is defined by secretion of a significant amount of pro-inflammatory cytokines: TNFα and IL-1β enhanced endocytosis and ability to kill intracellular pathogens (Adams, 1989; Martinez et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to studies that characterized M1 macrophages.

claim: M2 macrophages exhibit decreased expression of protein membrane markers, such as CD14 and CCR5, and increased fibronectin-1 production.
source: M2 macrophages exhibit decreased expression of protein membrane markers, such as CD14 and CCR5, and increased fibronectin-1 production.
evidence: This is established knowledge about M2 macrophage characteristics.

claim: M2 macrophages are characterized by the downregulation of pro-inflammatory cytokines.
source: In addition, M2 macrophages are also characterised by the downregulation of pro-inflammatory cytokines (Wang et al., 1998; Gratchev et al., 2001; Martinez et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to studies that characterized M2 macrophages.

claim: IFNγ-activated human macrophages (IFNγ-M1) are primed for enhanced inflammatory responses by stabilising HIF1α levels, activation of the JAK-STAT pathway, and increased production of IL-1β, all of which are dependent on enhanced levels of glycolysis.
source: IFNγ-activated human macrophages (IFNγ-M1) are primed for enhanced inflammatory responses by stabilising HIF1α levels, activation of the JAK-STAT pathway, and increased production of IL-1β, all of which are dependent on enhanced levels of glycolysis (Wang et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a study that established this mechanism.

claim: IL-4-M2 macrophages are defined by an intact tricarboxylic acid cycle (TCA), enhanced OxPhos, increased fatty acid synthesis (FAS), and fatty acid oxidation (FAO).
source: Alternatively activated human anti-inflammatory macrophages, most often observed in vitro through stimulation with IL-4 (IL-4-M2), are defined by an intact tricarboxylic acid cycle (TCA), enhanced OxPhos, increased fatty acid synthesis (FAS), and fatty acid oxidation (FAO) (O'Neill et al., 2016, Van den Bossche et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to studies that characterized IL-4-M2 macrophages.

claim: IFNγ-M1 macrophages are more active in glycolysis, while IL-4-M2 macrophages are more dependent on oxidative phosphorylation for their energy production.
source: In a nutshell, IFNγ-M1 macrophages are more active in glycolysis, while IL-4-M2 macrophages are more dependent on oxidative phosphorylation for their energy production.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on established knowledge about macrophage metabolism.

claim: A slightly higher amount of TNFα production was obtained for IFNγ-M1 when compared with IL-4-M2 macrophages.
source: A slightly higher amount of TNFα production was obtained for IFNγ-M1 when compared with IL-4-M2 macrophages.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: A statistically higher production of IL-10 was measured in IL-4-M2 when compared with IFNγ-M1 and untreated macrophages.
source: Regarding IL-10, a statistically higher production was measured in IL-4-M2 when compared with IFNγ-M1 and untreated macrophages (Figure 2A and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D with statistical significance.

claim: A higher amount of CXCL9 and a statistically significant increase in CXCL10 in IFNγ-M1 macrophages were observed.
source: For gene expression, a higher amount of CXCL9 and a statistically significant increase in CXCL10 in IFNγ-M1 macrophages were observed (Figure 2B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental gene expression data shown in Figures 2B and 2C.

claim: MRC1 and CCL13 were further expressed in IL-4-M2 macrophages when compared with untreated and IFNγ-M1 macrophages.
source: In addition, MRC1 and CCL13 were further expressed in IL-4-M2 macrophages when compared with untreated and IFNγ-M1 macrophages (Figure 2E and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental gene expression data shown in Figures 2E and 2F.

claim: IFNγ-M1 macrophages exhibited a higher ECAR and lower OCR in response to the treatments added, whilst IL-4-M2 and untreated macrophages had lower ECAR and higher OCR.
source: IFNγ-M1 macrophages exhibited a higher ECAR and lower OCR in response to the treatments added, whilst IL-4-M2 and untreated macrophages had lower ECAR and higher OCR (Figure 2G and J).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental metabolic flux data shown in Figures 2G and 2J.

claim: IFNγ-M1 macrophages have a statistically significant increase of basal and max glycolysis when compared with untreated macrophages.
source: IFNγ-M1 macrophages have a statistically significant increase of basal and max glycolysis when compared with untreated macrophages (Figure 2H and I).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2H and 2I with statistical significance.

claim: IL-4-M2 macrophages have a statistically significant increase in max respiration when compared with untreated macrophages.
source: In addition, all macrophage types have similar basal respiration, whilst IL-4-M2 macrophages have a statistically significant increase in max respiration when compared with untreated macrophages (Figure 2K and L).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2L with statistical significance.

claim: All macrophage types have similar basal respiration.
source: In addition, all macrophage types have similar basal respiration, whilst IL-4-M2 macrophages have a statistically significant increase in max respiration when compared with untreated macrophages (Figure 2K and L).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2K.

claim: IFNγ-M1 macrophages have lower τ1, τ2, τavg, and ORR values when compared with IL-4-M2 macrophages.
source: IFNγ-M1 macrophages have lower τ1, τ2, τavg, and ORR values when compared with IL-4-M2 macrophages (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by 2P-FLIM data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: UMAP representation of 2P-FLIM variables acquired during FCCP treatment provides a separation between IFNγ-M1 and IL-4-M2 macrophages.
source: UMAP representation of 2P-FLIM variables acquired during FCCP treatment provides a separation between IFNγ-M1 and IL-4-M2 macrophages (Figure 3F).
evidence: This claim is supported by UMAP visualization shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Random forests classification models achieved an ROC-AUC value of 0.944 when classifying macrophage polarisation from 2P-FLIM variables when treated with FCCP.
source: ROC curves of our dataset reveal high accuracy for predicting macrophage polarisation in the full FOV during FCCP (AUC = 0.944), when using 2P-FLIM variables as predictors (Figure 3G).
evidence: This claim is supported by machine learning analysis results shown in Figure 3G and Table 1.

claim: The random forests model for full field-of-view analysis had an OOB error rate of 16.67%.
evidence: This claim is supported by the machine learning model performance data shown in Table 1.

claim: τ1, τ2, and τavg are the most important 2P-FLIM variables for macrophage classification and data segregation.
source: Next, the mean decrease accuracy and mean decrease Gini returned by the random forests model reveal that τ1, τ2, and τavg are the most important 2P-FLIM variables for macrophage classification and data segregation (Figure 3H).
evidence: This claim is supported by feature importance analysis from the random forests model shown in Figure 3H.

claim: When using only τ1, τ2, and τavg as the 2P-FLIM predictors for random forests training, a high prediction accuracy was still achieved (ROC-AUC = 0.934).
source: When using only τ1, τ2, and τavg as the 2P-FLIM predictors for random forests training, a high prediction accuracy was still achieved (ROC-AUC = 0.934) (Figure 3G).
evidence: This claim is supported by machine learning analysis results shown in Figure 3G.

claim: Single-cell classification performance is affected by donor variability during the FCCP treatment.
source: From Figure 4C and Table 2, it is noticeable that single-cell classification performance is affected by donor variability during the FCCP treatment.
evidence: This claim is supported by the variation in ROC-AUC values across donors shown in Figure 4C and Table 2.

claim: Donors D and E have the highest ROC-AUC values and lowest OOB errors for single-cell classification.
source: Donors D and E have the highest ROC-AUC values and lowest OOB errors.
evidence: This claim is supported by the donor-specific machine learning results shown in Table 2.

claim: τ1, τ2, τavg, and α2 are the most important variables for classifying macrophage type at a single-cell level.
source: Finally, for the trained random forests models, we plotted the relative importance of each 2P-FLIM variable, and found that τ1, τ2, τavg, and α2 are the most important variables for classifying macrophage type at a single-cell level (Figure 4D and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by feature importance analysis from the random forests models shown in Figures 4D and 4E.

claim: FCCP functions as an uncoupler of mitochondria inner membrane allowing unhinged proton flux to the mitochondria matrix.
source: FCCP functions as an uncoupler of mitochondria inner membrane allowing unhinged proton flux to the mitochondria matrix.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the mechanism of action of FCCP.

claim: Proton flux due to FCCP causes a reduction of mitochondrial pH, increasing effectively the fluorescence lifetime of NAD(P)H.
source: Consequently, this proton flux causes a reduction of mitochondrial pH, increasing effectively the fluorescence lifetime of NAD(P)H.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the known mechanism of FCCP and is supported by citations.

claim: Schaefer et al. reported an increased NAD(P)H fluorescence lifetime due to reduced mitochondria pH elicited by FCCP treatment.
source: The unhinged proton flux due to FCCP compliments existing studies whereby Schaefer et al. reported an increased NAD(P)H fluorescence lifetime due to reduced mitochondria pH elicited by FCCP treatment (Blinova et al., 2005; Schaefer et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: FCCP treatment causes an increase in ETC activity indicated by increased oxygen consumption of IL-4-M2 macrophages.
source: Another consequence of FCCP treatment is an increase in ETC activity indicated by increased oxygen consumption of IL-4-M2 macrophages (Figure 2J).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2J.

claim: FCCP induction of maximal ETC activity increases the demand for NADH and FADH2 causing a concomitant increase of the FAO and TCA cycle activity already upregulated in IL-4-M2 macrophages.
source: FCCP induction of maximal ETC activity increases the demand for NADH and FADH2 causing a concomitant increase of the FAO and TCA cycle activity already upregulated in IL-4-M2 macrophages (Ludtmann et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is based on inference from metabolic pathways and is supported by a citation.

claim: The increased demand for NADH and FADH2 due to FCCP results in a reduced pool of FAD+ and an increase of NADH, effectively reducing ORR.
source: This demand results in a reduced pool of FAD+ and an increase of NADH, effectively reducing ORR (Ludtmann et al., 2014; Akie and Cooper, 2015; Viola et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is based on inference from metabolic pathways and is supported by citations.

claim: The higher heterogeneity in FCCP response is due to the effect of FCCP on the mitochondrial membrane and the higher dependence of FAS/FAO on IL-4-M2 macrophages basally.
source: The higher heterogeneity in FCCP response is due to the effect of FCCP on the mitochondrial membrane and the higher dependence of FAS/FAO on IL-4-M2 macrophages basally (O'Neill et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the observed data and is supported by a citation.

claim: IFNγ-M1 macrophages' lower dependence on ETC, TCA, FAO, and lower mitochondria membrane potential while producing most of ATP by glycolysis makes the impact of FCCP on the mitochondria and fluorescence lifetimes less pronounced.
source: Regarding IFNγ-M1 macrophages, their lower dependence on ETC, TCA, FAO, and lower mitochondria membrane potential while producing most of ATP by glycolysis makes the impact of FCCP on the mitochondria and fluorescence lifetimes less pronounced.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the metabolic characteristics of IFNγ-M1 macrophages.

claim: 2P-FLIM imaging has several advantages when compared with traditional metabolic assays and methods to classify and validate macrophage metabolism.
source: 2P-FLIM imaging has several advantages when compared with traditional metabolic assays and methods to classify and validate macrophage metabolism.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the advantages described in the manuscript.

claim: 2P-FLIM enables spatial and temporal resolution in a non-invasive manner, allowing single-cell and cell-to-cell evaluations into cellular heterogeneity in a basal and interrogated mode.
source: 2P-FLIM enables spatial and temporal resolution in a non-invasive manner, allowing single-cell and cell-to-cell evaluations into cellular heterogeneity in a basal and interrogated mode.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental approach and results presented in the manuscript.

claim: 2P-FLIM requires no fixation nor staining of cells and can be performed in real time with only a small number of cells.
source: 2P-FLIM requires no fixation nor staining of cells and can be performed in real time with only a small number of cells.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the advantages of 2P-FLIM methodology.

claim: This study demonstrates the feasibility of using 2P-FLIM as a tool to distinguish and classify opposing human macrophage polarisation states based on cellular metabolism and fluorescence lifetimes variables.
source: In this work, we demonstrated the feasibility of using 2P-FLIM as a tool to distinguish and classify opposing human macrophage polarisation states based on cellular metabolism and fluorescence lifetimes variables.
evidence: This is a summary claim supported by all the experimental data and analyses presented in the manuscript.

claim: Visualisation of the data showed a clear clustering pattern of IFNγ-M1 and IL-4-M2 macrophages in response to FCCP during real-time imaging in a full FoV.
source: Visualisation of the data showed a clear clustering pattern of IFNγ-M1 and IL-4-M2 macrophages in response to FCCP during real-time imaging in a full FoV.
evidence: This claim is supported by the UMAP visualization shown in Figure 3F.

claim: The excellent performance of machine learning models, applied on the data extracted from the non-invasive technique, underlines further the efficiency of this workflow.
source: The excellent performance of machine learning models, applied on the data extracted from the non-invasive technique, underlines further the efficiency of this workflow.
evidence: This claim is supported by the high ROC-AUC values and low OOB error rates achieved by the random forests models.

claim: This workflow can be easily adapted to non-invasively characterising macrophage polarisation in in vivo models and in vitro multicellular organoid models.
source: This workflow can be easily adapted to non-invasively characterising macrophage polarisation in in vivo models and in vitro multicellular organoid models.
evidence: This is a speculative claim about potential future applications of the methodology.

claim: These organoid models can be developed to study foreign body interactions, biomaterial assessment, pharmaceutical research and screening, and clinical applications such as disease diagnosis.
source: These organoid models can be developed to study foreign body interactions, biomaterial assessment, pharmaceutical research and screening, and clinical applications such as disease diagnosis.
evidence: This is a speculative claim about potential future applications of the methodology.

claim: The purity of CD14+CD11b+ macrophages was routinely >95%.
source: The purity of CD14+CD11b+ macrophages was assessed by flow cytometry and was routinely >95%.
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry measurements performed in the study.

claim: All of the fluorescence lifetime fitting values with χ2 < 1.3 were considered as 'good' fits.
source: In this study, all of the fluorescence lifetime fitting values with χ2 < 1.3 were considered as 'good' fits.
evidence: This is a methodological criterion established for data quality control in this study.

claim: Two-photon excitation of NAD(P)H and FAD+ fluorescence was performed at the excitation wavelength of 760 and 800 nm, respectively.
source: Two-photon excitation of NAD(P)H and FAD+ fluorescence was performed at the excitation wavelength of 760 and 800 nm, respectively.
evidence: This is a methodological detail describing the experimental setup.

claim: A 458/64 nm and 520/35 nm bandpass filter were used to isolate the NAD(P)H and FAD+ fluorescence emissions based on their emission spectra.
source: A 458/64 nm and 520/35 nm bandpass filter were used to isolate the NAD(P)H and FAD+ fluorescence emissions based on their emission spectra (Huang et al., 2002).
evidence: This is a methodological detail describing the experimental setup, supported by a citation.

claim: 512 × 512 pixel images were acquired with a pixel dwell time of 3.81 μs and 30 s collection time.
source: 512 × 512 pixel images were acquired with a pixel dwell time of 3.81 μs and 30 s collection time.
evidence: This is a methodological detail describing the imaging parameters.

claim: Fluorescence lifetime images with their associated decay curves for NAD(P)H were obtained with a minimum of 1 × 106 photons peak.
source: Fluorescence lifetime images with their associated decay curves for NAD(P)H were obtained with a minimum of 1 × 106 photons peak.
evidence: This is a methodological detail describing the data acquisition criteria.

claim: The α1 variable was removed from the random forests model due to its deterministic relationship with the α2 variable.
source: The α1 variable was removed from the random forests model due to its deterministic relationship with the α2 variable (Figure 3—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is a methodological decision supported by the correlation analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 5.

claim: Support vector machine (SVM) and logistic regression models yielded similar performance with 87.5% accuracy when dividing the full FoV datapoints into 80% training and 20% testing dataset.
source: Support vector machine (SVM) and logistic regression models were also implemented for comparing with the random forests model and yielded similar performance with 87.5% accuracy when dividing the full FoV datapoints into 80% training and 20% testing dataset.
evidence: This claim is supported by comparative machine learning analysis performed in the study.

claim: Neither the SVM model nor the logistic model is able to provide information on the relative importance of the predictors.
source: However, neither the SVM model nor the logistic model is able to provide information on the relative importance of the predictors, and they both require an independent dataset for model validation.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the limitations of SVM and logistic regression models.

claim: Random forests is especially suitable for small datasets, where we do not have additional data for validating the model.
source: This makes random forests especially suitable for small datasets, where we do not have additional data for validating the model.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the advantages of random forests for small datasets.

claim: An ROC-AUC value less than 0.5 suggests no discrimination, 0.7–0.8 is considered acceptable, 0.8–0.9 is considered excellent, and more than 0.9 is considered outstanding.
source: An ROC-AUC value less than 0.5 suggests no discrimination, 0.7–0.8 is considered acceptable, 0.8–0.9 is considered excellent, and more than 0.9 is considered outstanding (Mandrekar, 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge about ROC-AUC interpretation, supported by a citation.

claim: This study establishes 2P-FLIM as a method to discriminate IFNγ-M1 and IL-4-M2 macrophages, which is most pronounced by macrophages' differential responses when treated with carbonyl cyanide-p-trifluoromethoxyphenylhydrazone (FCCP).
source: This study establishes 2P-FLIM as a method to discriminate IFNγ-M1 and IL-4-M2 macrophages, which is most pronounced by macrophages' differential responses when treated with carbonyl cyanide-p-trifluoromethoxyphenylhydrazone (FCCP).
evidence: This is a summary claim supported by the experimental data showing best separation during FCCP treatment.

claim: This work reports, for the first time, the classification of human macrophages by random forests using data obtained from real-time metabolic perturbations triggered during 2P-FLIM.
source: Our work reports, for the first time, the classification of human macrophages by random forests using data obtained from real-time metabolic perturbations triggered during 2P-FLIM.
evidence: This is a novelty claim based on the unique combination of methods used in this study.

claim: There is an increasing trend of τavg in response to the application metabolic enzymatic inhibitors, with the exception of 2-DG, in which a decrease of τavg was observed for both macrophage phenotypes.
source: We derived the average fluorescence lifetime (τavg) and ORR of IFNγ-M1 and IL-4-M2 macrophages from the full FoV of 2P-FLIM data and observed an increasing trend of τavg in response to the application metabolic enzymatic inhibitors. With the exception of 2-DG, in which a decrease of τavg was observed for both macrophage phenotypes (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by the time-course data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: There is a slight decreasing trend of ORR, followed by a raise in ORR with the 2-DG treatment for IFNγ-M1 macrophages.
source: Regarding ORR, there is a slight decreasing trend of ORR, followed by a raise in ORR with the 2-DG treatment for IFNγ-M1 macrophages.
evidence: This claim is supported by the time-course data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: For IL-4-M2 macrophages, there is a decrease in ORR with the oligomycin treatment, followed by stabilisation with FCCP and Rot + AA, and finally an increase elicited by 2-DG.
source: For IL-4-M2 macrophages, there is a decrease in ORR with the oligomycin treatment, followed by stabilisation with FCCP and Rot + AA, and finally an increase elicited by 2-DG (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by the time-course data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: A reduced τavg, observed with IFNγ-M1 macrophages, reflects a higher relative amount of free NAD(P)H (which has characteristic short fluorescence lifetimes), indicative of glycolysis.
source: A reduced τavg, observed with IFNγ-M1 macrophages, reflects a higher relative amount of free NAD(P)H (which has characteristic short fluorescence lifetimes), indicative of glycolysis (Walsh et al., 2013; Perottoni et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is based on inference from FLIM data and is supported by citations.

claim: IL-4-M2 macrophages had higher τavg-reflective of OxPhos due to increased proportion of longer lifetime, protein-bound NAD(P)H.
source: In contrast, IL-4-M2 macrophages had higher τavg-reflective of OxPhos due to increased proportion of longer lifetime, protein-bound NAD(P)H (Okkelman et al., 2019, Walsh et al., 2020; Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is based on inference from FLIM data and is supported by citations.

claim: A lower ORR reflects a higher fraction of NAD(P)H and a lower FAD+ associated with upregulation of OxPhos.
source: Varying interpretations of ORR are reported in previous studies (Varone et al., 2014; Walsh et al., 2020), and for this study, we adopt a lower ORR reflecting a higher fraction of NAD(P)H and a lower FAD+ associated with upregulation of OxPhos (Equation 3; Neto et al., 2020).
evidence: This is an interpretation adopted for this study, supported by citations.

claim: IL-4-M2 macrophages exhibited a lower ORR across the treatments in contrast with IFNγ-M1 macrophages, validating a higher dependency of IL-4-M2 macrophages on OxPhos when compared with IFNγ-M1 macrophages.
source: IL-4-M2 macrophages exhibited a lower ORR across the treatments in contrast with IFNγ-M1 macrophages, validating a higher dependency of IL-4-M2 macrophages on OxPhos when compared with IFNγ-M1 macrophages.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the ORR data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: There is a noticeable increase in τ1, τ2, and τavg and an appreciable decrease in ORR in IL-4-M2 macrophages when compared with IFNγ-M1-treated macrophages.
source: With IL-4-M2 macrophages, there is a noticeable increase in τ1, τ2, and τavg and an appreciable decrease in ORR when compared with IFNγ-M1-treated macrophages.
evidence: This claim is supported by the heatmap data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The trending increase of NAD(P)H fluorescence lifetimes is further exacerbated after treatment with FCCP in IL-4-M2 macrophages.
source: The trending increase of NAD(P)H fluorescence lifetimes is further exacerbated after treatment with FCCP in IL-4-M2 macrophages.
evidence: This claim is supported by the heatmap data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: During stem cell osteogenic differentiation, Guo et al. tested oligomycin A (mitochondrial respiration inhibitor) as an experimental treatment in parallel to standard osteogenic media and observed a decrease in NAD(P)H average lifetime reflective of reduced oxidative phosphorylation.
source: For instance, during stem cell osteogenic differentiation, Guo et al. tested oligomycin A (mitochondrial respiration inhibitor) as an experimental treatment in parallel to standard osteogenic media. A decrease in NAD(P)H average lifetime was calculated reflective of reduced oxidative phosphorylation.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Oligomycin A treatment promoted an increase in lactate production, lower oxygen consumption, and lower osteogenic differentiation.
source: In addition, oligomycin A treatment promoted an increase in lactate production, lower oxygen consumption, and lower osteogenic differentiation (Guo et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The separation between IFNγ-M1 and IL-4-M2 macrophages is observed when applying PCA analysis on FCCP treated human macrophages.
source: This segregation is also observed when applying PCA analysis on FCCP treated human macrophages.
evidence: This claim is supported by the PCA visualization shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: The separation between IFNγ-M1 and IL-4-M2 macrophages is not observed for t-SNE analysis.
source: However, this separation is not observed for t-SNE analysis (Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by the t-SNE visualization shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: Phasor analysis demonstrates a higher segregation of IFNγ-M1 and IL-4-M2 macrophages when using FCCP treatment.
source: In addition, our phasor analysis (Figure 3—figure supplement 3) also demonstrates a higher segregation of IFNγ-M1 and IL-4-M2 macrophages when using FFCP treatment.
evidence: This claim is supported by the phasor analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: The limitation in pre-defining values for the fluorescence lifetime variables such as τ1 and τ2 can mask important predictors for the classification problem.
source: Albeit, the limitation in pre-defining values for the fluorescence lifetime variables such as τ1 and τ2 can mask important predictors for the classification problem.
evidence: This is a speculative claim about the limitations of phasor analysis.

claim: Higher NAD(P)H fluorescence lifetimes such as τ1, τ2, and τavg are attributable to two major factors: increases in NADPH concentrations and microenvironmental shifts.
source: Higher NAD(P)H fluorescence lifetimes such as τ1, τ2, and τavg are attributable to two major factors: increases in NADPH concentrations and microenvironmental shifts (Blacker et al., 2014; Schaefer et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: There is some cell-to-cell variability which could stem from the uptake capacity of FCCP and other treatments in our experiments as well as the underlying health of the donors which is not available.
source: There is some cell-to-cell variability which could stem from the uptake capacity of FCCP and other treatments in our experiments as well as the underlying health of the donors which is not available (Smiley et al., 1991; Stiebing et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a speculative claim about potential sources of variability, supported by citations.

claim: Future efforts to improve single-cell classification include increasing the overall number of cells analysed to ensure a stronger classification.
source: Future efforts to improve single-cell classification include increasing the overall number of cells analysed to ensure a stronger classification.
evidence: This is a speculative claim about future improvements to the methodology.

claim: By observing phenotypic IFNγ-M1 and IL-4-M2 macrophage cell surface markers during the imaging process by immunofluorescence or other modes of tagging, it would be possible to improve the classification efficiency.
source: In addition, by observing phenotypic IFNγ-M1 and IL-4-M2 macrophage cell surface markers (examples include CD80, CD86, CD163, and CD206, respectively) during the imaging process by immunofluorescence or other modes of tagging, it would be possible to improve the classification efficiency (Murray et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a speculative claim about potential improvements to the methodology, supported by a citation.
